items.title: Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2022
items.q: think if Keith Moon played jazz

ctx.x: The other thing just in general is that the pianist in our group, Chuck Lamb, and a guitarist, Mike DeMicco and Dan and I, it’s a highly democratic process you know. So when we put out a record or when we do a concert, it is sort of like a Venn diagram of all the things that we happen to think is cool, probably much to our commercial demise you know, well in terms of like for example none of us wants to make a record that sounds anything like any Kenny G record. Sorry, Kenny. Or any of the hundreds of sax players…

for “Kathy’s Waltz” it’s just interesting to think of when “Kathy’s Waltz” was written reggae didn’t even exist. You know? So because our dad went out to the Middle East and he incorporated music that didn’t exist in the United States like the Turkish beat that became “Blue Rondo” I feel like he sort of gave us the grand rights to explore and put other music into our re-interpretations of his music. If he were our age he’d be doing it. And the other thing is because of our age we all have a rock & roll kind of…
Yeah, I’ve heard that like you’re still playing straight eighth notes. Like with the older fellas like in a big band. And you give them a rock number and they’re still swinging.
